entityDescription:
The Würzburg-Schweinfurt University of Applied Sciences (THWS) is one of the largest universities of applied sciences in Bavaria. On the following pages, you will find all the important information about the THWS (https://www.thws.de/hochschule/profil-der-thws/), which is distinguished by a wide range of practice-oriented degree programs as well as by its research activities, internationalization, digitalization, and an extensive continuing education program. You can get a sense of the Würzburg-Schweinfurt University of Applied Sciences through facts and figures, videos, and our university magazine “Fokus Orange.”
THWS is located at two campuses in northern Bavaria, in the cities of Würzburg and Schweinfurt. The faculties and their degree programs are housed in various buildings; their locations can be found in the overview of university buildings.

entityDescription:
For 45 years, Stichting De Noordzee (The North Sea Foundation) has been committed to protecting the largest natural area of the Netherlands: the North Sea. We stand for a clean and healthy North Sea that is used sustainably. We work towards a healthy ecosystem that is resilient and adapts to external influences. North Sea nature must always be the foundation for sustainable use. We advocate for the North Sea and collaborate with other stakeholders to find solutions for current and future challenges.

Three core roles are central to our work
- Agendasetting of pressing issues and solutions;
- Collaboration within the (international) level playing field;
- Accelerating the research – policy interface
We bring these roles into practice by partnering with policymakers, (energy) sectors and operators, funders, the scientific community, and by reaching out to the general public. Our key influence lies in firmly anchored North Sea marine, spatial and nature protection policies and regulation – based on the latest scientific insights. Therefore we actively focus on national and international policy advocacy and communication. Since pressing issues do cross borders, we focus on the North Sea Basin level, stressing the importance of international marine policy cooperation and regulation. 
To realize our mission, we work on four core strategic themes: nature protection, sustainable fisheries, nature-friendly energy, and a clean sea. The nature protection program aims to safeguard large areas of the sea from human activity, allowing species space to recover – free from disturbance. In connection with this, we promote sustainable fishing practices and improved ecosystem-based fisheries management. The nature-friendly energy program is based on the idea that the North Sea is central to the energy transition, and the sustainable energy transition at sea must mitigate environmental risks and ensure nature protection and enhancement. Finally, a healthy North Sea is a clean sea – free from visible and invisible marine litter.

entityDescription:
Prepared International (PPI) specializes in consultancy, research and training services in the field of Disaster Risk Reduction, Preparedness and Resilience, in order to inform political decision-making and to provide effective capacity-building strategies in the long term. The PPI approach encompasses a holistic set of tools for approaching Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), including the development of preparedness models, organizational development and restructuring, self-adaptive systems, and strategies for governance and mass evacuation. 
As guiding mission PPI seeks to offer detailed, specialized expertise in the field of Disaster Management to design strategies for resilience that are both practical and detailed. This includes Operational Continuity Management for urban areas, developing and mature economies, strategies for high-risk zones, and cooperation in Disaster Risk Management for conflicting communities, including in post-conflict regions. PPI also offers long-standing expertise in simulation design and capacity-building strategies. Our team of international and local experts works towards applying lessons gathered at the forefront while developing and implementing new concepts and tools, such as the new concept of United Nations Disaster Assessment and Coordination (UNDAC) Disaster Response Preparedness Missions, the development and implementation of the mission methodology for Mass Evacuations in Natural Disasters (MEND) Preparedness Missions, or the application of the stress-test methodology. Our long-standing experience in capacity assessments and investment planning was developed in missions for the UNDAC Disaster Preparedness System, UNDP, EU or national systems; therefore, systemic Emergency and Preparedness assessment methodologies like the World Bank’s Ready to Response (R2R) concept fits perfectly in our portfolio and services. In 2020, PPI developed a methodology to analyze the ability of a EP&R system to fight pandemics based on the R2R methodology.
Our experience features a strong regional focus on the Western Balkans, with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) as a point of reference both during assessments and in our recommendations for future development. In addition, PPI is part of the Advisory Group to the Disaster Preparedness and Prevention Initiative (DPPI SEE), which offers valuable knowledge on the broader region. The team suggested for this assignment consists of recognized international experts and a leading country expert. Their valuable experience will facilitate an effective and efficient assessment process, build on best practices and lead to concise recommendations tailored to the needs of Ukraine.
On top of our first-class regional and country expertise, a clear advantage of PPI is its recent experience in applying the R2R Diagnostic methodology to assess the Emergency Preparedness and Response systems of Cabo Verde and six Western Balkan states resulting in PPI experts having detailed and updated knowledge on how to implement similar tools and conduct investment planning. The fact that all countries were very pleased with the diagnostic results and recommendations made by PPI is a clear indication of the company´s ability and capacities to deliver similar assignments to the satisfaction of all stakeholders involved.
While the organization is registered under German law in the State of Bavaria (HRB 27352), the highly experienced staff is multi-national and include key local experts. All our colleagues are driven by the same understanding, namely that stronger preparedness of communities and societies is possible with the current investments in this field. In 2023, PPI received as first private organization the Special Recognition of the Averted Disaster Award, and in 2024, no less than 11 PPI colleagues received the UN Heroes Award.

entityDescription:
Calsens is a Spanish engineering company specializing in structural monitoring and optical sensor technology. Based in Spain, they provide 24/7 online monitoring services for civil and industrial structures, combining advanced sensor hardware with their own proprietary IoT software platform.
Their work falls across three main areas:
Structural Health Monitoring — Calsens deploys optical sensors to monitor the condition of infrastructure ranging from bridges and viaducts to pedestrian walkways. Monitoring can be short-term (a few hours, for a specific test) or permanent (continuous data collection and analysis over multiple years), supporting predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure.
Optical Sensor Development — The company designs and manufactures optical sensors for a wide range of applications, including FBG (Fibre Bragg Grating) sensors for strain measurement in civil engineering, high-temperature sensors for aerospace environments, pressure sensors for pressurized conduits, and pH sensors for concrete structures. R&D is central to their identity, with the team active in both academic and private research.
Load Testing & Structural Assessment — Calsens carries out static and dynamic load tests on civil and industrial structures, complemented by finite element numerical modelling, structural fitness reports, and engineering calculations.
Their portfolio includes projects on multiple bridges and viaducts across Spain (such as the Mascarat Bridge, Viaducto Las Rosas, Viaducto Río Algar, and others), and they collaborate with a range of companies and institutions across different sectors.

Arc develops lightweight requirements management software for agile space teams.
The platform replaces requirements spreadsheets, fragile file links and manual verification tracking with one structured workspace for requirements, architecture, systems and tests. It keeps requirements, interfaces, test cases, results and verification evidence connected as programmes change.
Arc uses Git-style branches to help engineers propose, review and approve changes safely. AI agents trace dependencies, check coverage and propose updates for engineers to review, while the team remains responsible for changes and approvals.
Arc supports role-based access, connected change history and traceable evidence for audit preparation. It can be hosted by Arc or deployed within customer-controlled infrastructure, including on-premise and firewall-contained environments.

Valve-Service Pein AG is a family-owned industrial service company specializing in the maintenance, repair, overhaul and testing of high-pressure valves and industrial valve systems.
Our core expertise lies in providing reliable technical service for critical valve applications, including inspection, disassembly, assessment, refurbishment, reassembly and pressure testing.
With our background in metal technology and high-pressure valve service, we support industrial customers where reliability, safety and technical quality are essential.
As part of our long-term development, we are expanding our expertise in advanced fluid-control applications, including hydrogen technologies and other demanding high-pressure systems.
We are interested in contributing our existing service and maintenance capabilities to the European space industry, particularly in areas related to high-pressure fluid systems, valves, test facilities and associated ground-support equipment.
Our objective is initially to participate as a specialized service and industrial partner and to cooperate with experienced companies and organizations within the European space ecosystem. Through such partnerships, we aim to further develop our technical capabilities and gradually expand into advanced applications relevant to space and other high-technology industries.

description:
Datum Vega is a Toulouse-based aerospace engineering company specializing in the development, structural analysis, verification, and qualification of spacecraft and space hardware. We support organizations in translating mission and system objectives into robust engineering requirements, verified designs, and qualified flight hardware.

Our team brings senior-level experience gained through work at Boeing, Northrop Grumman, and Airbus U.S. Space & Defense. Our expertise encompasses spacecraft structures, human spaceflight systems, finite element modeling, structural dynamics, static loads, vibration and shock, fatigue and fracture mechanics, optimization, margin-of-safety assessment, and qualification engineering.

Datum Vega also provides requirements, verification, and test support, including requirements traceability, verification planning, test planning and supervision, model correlation, qualification evidence, and flight-readiness support. Our Chronos initiative is a digital engineering platform designed to connect, execute, and preserve complex technical workflows while maintaining human engineering authority. Its developing toolset includes structural-analysis automation, joint and sandwich-panel analysis, material selection, and qualification evidence management.

Datum Vega serves space-sector organizations in Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States as a specialist engineering partner for demanding development and qualification programmes.

description:
SustainStruct UG is a German technology start-up developing space-enabled Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) solutions for bridges and other critical infrastructure. 

Based in Langen, Germany, the company is supported by the ESA Business Incubation Centre Hessen & Baden-Württemberg. Our approach combines satellite-based technologies, particularly GNSS and Earth Observation data such as SAR/InSAR, with in-situ structural sensors including accelerometers and environmental sensors. High-precision GNSS positioning is used to monitor structural displacement and provide an absolute positioning reference, complementing accelerometer-based measurements of dynamic structural behaviour. 

In parallel, we are exploring the integration of SAR/InSAR-derived deformation information to extend monitoring from individual sensor locations toward larger structures and infrastructure areas. SustainStruct develops the complete monitoring chain, including sensor and GNSS integration, edge data acquisition, secure data transmission, cloud-based processing, data analytics, and web-based visualization. 

By combining space-derived and terrestrial measurements, our goal is to support continuous condition monitoring, deformation analysis, anomaly detection, and ultimately predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure. The technology is currently being validated through a real bridge monitoring pilot in cooperation with academic and infrastructure partners, with the objective of developing scalable monitoring solutions for infrastructure owners, engineering companies, and asset operators.

entityDescription:
Netguru S.A. is an AI-native software engineering and product design company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Poznań, Poland, employing approximately 500 specialists. The company designs, builds and operates production artificial intelligence systems together with the software platforms around them, with a deliberate focus on established, asset-heavy industries where digital and AI adoption has historically lagged behind.
Core competencies cover applied AI engineering — large language model systems, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, computer vision, document understanding and evaluation frameworks — alongside full-cycle software delivery from discovery and architecture through implementation to long-term maintenance. Supporting competences include backend and distributed systems engineering, web, mobile and integration development, cloud and platform engineering on AWS, Azure and GCP, data engineering and analytics platforms, and digital product design. AI capability is not organised as a separate practice but applied as the default engineering method across the delivery organisation.
Netguru operates dedicated AI inference infrastructure independent of third-party model providers. GPU capacity is leased from European sovereign cloud and high-performance computing operators in Poland, and the company also deploys model serving on-premise inside a client's own network. This allows engagements to be executed without sending data outside a defined jurisdiction, and supports air-gapped or otherwise restricted environments where commercial model APIs cannot be used.
The client portfolio is concentrated in traditional and regulated sectors: industrial and manufacturing operations, energy and HVAC systems, medical technology and healthcare, logistics and field service, financial services, and enterprise commerce. Typical engagements connect AI and modern software to legacy estates — ERP and MES systems, installed hardware, field operations and long-lived operational data — under real constraints of safety, certification, data protection and system reliability.
Delivery is governed by a documented internal framework of standard operating procedures covering estimation, earned-value progress reporting, quality assurance, risk management, change control and security, with a named Delivery Manager, Engineering Manager and quality owner assigned to every engagement. The company maintains an ISO 27001-certified information security management system and is a certified B Corporation. All engineering, design and delivery personnel are employed or contracted within the European Union, and infrastructure, source code repositories and AI inference can be confined to EU-resident environments in line with GDPR and EU data sovereignty requirements.

Company description: Netguru S.A. is an AI-native software engineering and product design company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Poznań, Poland, employing approximately 500 specialists. The company designs, builds and operates production artificial intelligence systems together with the software platforms around them, with a deliberate focus on established, asset-heavy industries where digital and AI adoption has historically lagged behind.
Core competencies cover applied AI engineering — large language model systems, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, computer vision, document understanding and evaluation frameworks — alongside full-cycle software delivery from discovery and architecture through implementation to long-term maintenance. Supporting competences include backend and distributed systems engineering, web, mobile and integration development, cloud and platform engineering on AWS, Azure and GCP, data engineering and analytics platforms, and digital product design. AI capability is not organised as a separate practice but applied as the default engineering method across the delivery organisation.
Netguru operates dedicated AI inference infrastructure independent of third-party model providers. GPU capacity is leased from European sovereign cloud and high-performance computing operators in Poland, and the company also deploys model serving on-premise inside a client's own network. This allows engagements to be executed without sending data outside a defined jurisdiction, and supports air-gapped or otherwise restricted environments where commercial model APIs cannot be used.
The client portfolio is concentrated in traditional and regulated sectors: industrial and manufacturing operations, energy and HVAC systems, medical technology and healthcare, logistics and field service, financial services, and enterprise commerce. Typical engagements connect AI and modern software to legacy estates — ERP and MES systems, installed hardware, field operations and long-lived operational data — under real constraints of safety, certification, data protection and system reliability.
Delivery is governed by a documented internal framework of standard operating procedures covering estimation, earned-value progress reporting, quality assurance, risk management, change control and security, with a named Delivery Manager, Engineering Manager and quality owner assigned to every engagement. The company maintains an ISO 27001-certified information security management system and is a certified B Corporation. All engineering, design and delivery personnel are employed or contracted within the European Union, and infrastructure, source code repositories and AI inference can be confined to EU-resident environments in line with GDPR and EU data sovereignty requirements.
